technical.rationale: 模型流记账和子代理归集是相对宿主投影的机制增量，可复用思路，但依赖账本及价格。

business.rationale: 提供随会话查看成本的操作增量，仍以真实账单验收，节省未测。

recommendation.reason: 频繁切换模型并需要核对用量的人，可在隔离 DSH Profile 对照短任务。相比在多个界面切换，底栏把余额与会话用量放到输入区附近。实际账单、出站或更新状态不清楚时，停用并回到宿主及供应商账单。

scenario.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01) 覆盖频繁对账的具体摩擦，无用户需求实证。

advantage.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01) 聚合多字段超出布局调整，但不能代替账单。

evidence.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01) 和 [Q02](#research-q02) 追到流、价表、认证及更新，真实宿主未验。

A DeepSeek Harness plugin that adds an account information row under the composer: provider and model, real balance or subscription quota, peak/off-peak pricing, and what this session has cost. ![Bottom Info Bar in full mode](assets/bar-full.webp) ## What it shows The bar follows the active session and picks one of three readings per provider (mutually exclusive, nothing to switch by hand): **balance** shows the real balance from the provider's own API, **subscription quota** shows each quota window's remaining allowance with its reset countdown (an exhausted window stays visible at 0% instead of disappearing, flagged low), and **cloud billing** shows this month's real spend from the official billing API. On top of that come four spend tallies — this session, today, last 30 days, all time — plus extras such as time and custom text. All four come from the plugin's own ledger, which **starts counting when the plugin first runs**: calls made before that (or before you cleared the ledger) are not included, and hovering the spend writes out the exact start of the count. For the authoritative figure for a whole session, use the provider's own balance or bill. In balance mode, hovering the balance expands it into topped-up and granted balances, so gifted credit is never conflated with the money you paid in. On **DSH 0.2.2 with the native activity/usage buttons**, the native line sits on top and the plugin's account information on the line below. Clicking any plugin field still switches between **Full** and **Compact** with the same height/fade animation: Full shows the native line, Compact collapses it. The native buttons keep their own click behavior and open Harness's details dialogs. Each of the two native buttons can be hidden separately from the plugin's settings page. The context ring keeps its existing details and plugin settings. On **older hosts**, clicking the bar still switches between **Full** and **Compact**: Full keeps the legacy statistics row, Compact collapses it. Plugin fields remain identical in both modes. Compatibility is detected from the host's live extension entries, rather than a version string. ## Install Recommended: open the DSH plugin page, choose **Add plugin**, and enter the npm package name — DSH fetches the published package from npm, with no commands and no build: ``` dsh-bottom-info-bar ``` Prefer the terminal? The same install from the command line: ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-bottom-info-bar ``` To run the newest code from the default branch instead of the latest release, paste the repository URL into the same field: ``` https://github.com/songoao25/dsh-bottom-info-bar ``` Then **restart DSH** — plugins are composed when the host starts, so a page refresh is not enough. In the desktop app, use **Plugins → Add plugin**; its profile is managed by the app and cannot be installed into through the CLI. Other install methods (including Windows PowerShell) and troubleshooting: [docs/INSTALL.md](docs/INSTALL.md). The context usage ring keeps the native hover tooltip and opens a statistics panel when clicked. Both overlays render outside the bottom bar so they do not change its contents. ## Settings Plugin settings live under **Plugins → bottom-info-bar** and save as you change them. The page is built on the same card system DSH 0.2.2 uses elsewhere: every section is one card with a title and a one-line summary, separated by whitespace instead of dividers. **Information to show** holds every field switch and color, grouped into native information and plugin information — both collapsible, with search across all rows. Notices render on the bar as soft pills and no longer have switches. **Quota credentials** stays collapsed by default, **billing data** covers export and clear, and **version & updates** holds the update mode with rollback. Resetting fields or colors does not change Harness's native button preferences. ![Information to show: every field switch and color, grouped and collapsible](assets/settings-plugin.webp) Plugin information is further grouped by billing mode — read only the block that matches your provider; each block's heading says which items carry data for it. Time and date, subscription window percentage direction, quota credentials and billing data are separate cards: ![Time and date: time zones only](assets/settings-time.webp) API keys go in DSH under **Settings → Models**; subscriptions (Codex, OpenCode, Xiaomi Token Plan, Command Code, MiniMax, Zhipu GLM, Kimi For Coding) read the local sign-in or the model key already configured in DSH (MiniMax's needs to be a Subscription Key). Unused plans never show up, and nothing needs to be typed on the plugin page. The one exception is Alibaba Token Plan (China and international sites): the inference plan key cannot read quota, so set an Alibaba Cloud AccessKey (`ALIBABA_CLOUD_ACCESS_KEY_ID` / `ALIBABA_CLOUD_ACCESS_KEY_SECRET`, a RAM user is enough) under **Quota credentials** in the plugin settings (collapsed by default), or in DSH's credentials / same-named environment variables. Anything off the list gets a not-supported hint instead of borrowed numbers. ## Spend and updates The ledger requires a DSH runtime with Node.js 22.13 or newer. It keeps records and historical session indexes in a local disk database, reads bounded batches, and streams exports. Existing ledger files are migrated once and retained for recovery; see [Ledger storage and recovery](docs/LEDGER.md). Every model response records one entry (usage × unit price, locked the moment the response completes) and survives restarts. The plugin checks npm once per DSH start: **automatic updates** (default) download in the background and take effect after you restart, **manual updates** only notify; a bad release can be rolled back from settings. The ledger stores tokens and amounts, never conversation content; data stays under this end's `DSH_HOME` in `dsh-bottom-info-bar/` (default `~/.dsh/dsh-bottom-info-bar/`, overridable via `DSH_BOTTOM_INFO_BAR_DATA_DIR`) and survives uninstall — export or clear it from Billing data if you want a clean slate. ## Uninstall and roll back Remove the plugin on the DSH plugin page (or `dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-bottom-info-bar`) and restart DSH: the native stats row comes back by itself and no plugin files are left behind. The ledger is kept on purpose — export or clear it from **Billing data** before removing the plugin if you want a clean slate. To go back a version instead, the update section offers **roll back to the previous version** while a newer build is waiting for a restart, and after a failed update. Details: [docs/INSTALL.md](docs/INSTALL.md). ## FAQ **The bar shows "not configured" or "Refresh failed" — is it broken?** No. When it can't read data, the bar keeps the last good snapshot and never shows a fake 0%.
